knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Curl of a Vector Field

question.:question/problem: Given that $F(x,y,z)=1{z}^{2}\,i+2y\,j+k,$ what is $\text{curl}\,F?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j+R\,k$ is a vector field on ${R}^{3}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the curl of $F$ is the vector field given by

$$
curl\,F=∇\times F=|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ P & Q & R\end{aligned}|.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{curl}\,F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ 1{z}^{2} & 2y & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(1)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(2y)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(1)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(1{z}^{2})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(1{z}^{2})]k \\  & =(0-0)i-(0-2z)j+(0-0)k \\  & =2z\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Consider the vector field $F={e}^{y+z}\,i+j+xyz\,k.$ Evaluate $∇\times F$ at the point  $(2,1,-1).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j+R\,k$ is a vector field on ${R}^{3}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the curl of $F$ is the vector field given by

$$
curl\,F=∇\times F=|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ P & Q & R\end{aligned}|.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{curl}\,F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ {e}^{y+z} & 1 & xyz\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(xyz)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(1)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xyz)-\frac{∂}{∂z}({e}^{y+z})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(1)-\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{y+z})]k \\  & =(xz-0)i-(yz-{e}^{y+z})j+(0-{e}^{y+z})k \\  & =xz\,i+({e}^{y+z}-yz)j-{e}^{y+z}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate $\text{curl}\,F$ at the point $(2,1,-1),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(\text{curl}\,F)(2,1,-1) & =2(-1)\,i+({e}^{1+(-1)}-1(-1))j-{e}^{1+(-1)}\,k \\  & =-2\,i+2\,j-k.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Consider the vector field $F=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\,i+y{z}^{2}\,j+(x-z)\,k.$ Evaluate $∇\times F$ at the point  $(2,-1,3).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j+R\,k$ is a vector field on ${R}^{3}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the curl of $F$ is the vector field given by

$$
curl\,F=∇\times F=|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ P & Q & R\end{aligned}|.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{curl}\,F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y) & y{z}^{2} & (x-z)\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(x-z)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(y{z}^{2})]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(x-z)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y))]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(y{z}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y))]k \\  & =(0-2yz)i-(1-0)j+(0-\frac{1}{x+y})k \\  & =-2yz\,i-j-\frac{1}{x+y}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate $\text{curl}\,F$ at the point $(2,-1,3),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(\text{curl}\,F)(2,-1,3) & =-2(-1)(3)\,i-j-\frac{1}{2+(-1)}\,k \\  & =6\,i-j-k.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Consider the vector field $F={x}^{2}\,i+xz\,j+{z}^{2}\,k.$ Evaluate $∇\times F$ at the point  $(-4,-3,1).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j+R\,k$ is a vector field on ${R}^{3}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the curl of $F$ is the vector field given by

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{curl}\,F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ {x}^{2} & xz & {z}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}({z}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xz)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}({z}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xz)-\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2})]k \\  & =(0-x)i-(0-0)j+(z-0)k \\  & =-x\,i+z\,k.\end{aligned}
